Proved for every open U, not only ⊤: rationalLine.openDiamond U p q = ∅ (an irrational point of J_U(p, q) equals p, rationalLine_eq_of_le_irrational, and every open interval holds two distinct irrationals). readme_row: | `Causal.RationalLineExtras` | — | ETT programme, layer 1 (T-abs-rational-line-extras): the rational line's other ladder facts: a time function (the identity), strongly causal in the open form (intervals are causally convex), absolutely minimal on every open set for every cover; not locally causally open in the future (`causal_ladder`: absolute minimality and ¬ causally open in the future), not tarentin (no diamond has interior), not causally plain, no chronal neighbours, not causally compact (`J(p, q) = ℚ ∩ [p, q]`); conjoined in `rationalLine_separates`, valid in either reading of `defi:causalite`; 2026-11-21 |
kb_proposals: 0079 (or the next free id), pattern — The rational line in the ladder: an irrational point is ≤-related to itself only (Causal.rationalLine_eq_of_le_irrational), so no diamond has interior (rationalLine_openDiamond: not tarentin) and J(0, 1) = ℚ ∩ [0, 1] is not closed (rationalLine_diamond_top: not causally compact); with ≪ empty, not plain and no chronal neighbours; a time function (id) and open strong causality (intervals). It is absolutely minimal on every open for every cover (rationalLine_absolutelyMinimalOn), so Causal.rationalLine_separates is the either-reading witness for X ⇏ locally_causally_open(_future) and, with time_function and strongly_causal_open in `from`, for X ⇏ causally_open(_future), causally_arc_connected (T-abs-rational-line-extras).

pattern — A ladder failure read backwards through a conjunctive edge is one causal_ladder call: `intro h; have := hOther; exact hNot (by causal_ladder)` (rationalLine_not_locallyCausallyOpenFuture: absolutely_minimal ∧ locally_causally_open_future ⇒ causally_open_future). The other premise must be a hypothesis in context (a `have`), since causal_ladder uses no lemma that is not a rule (kb/0048) (T-abs-rational-line-extras).
